data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German elements hoff (hof) meaning 'court, farm, household' and mann (mann) meaning 'man'. Thus, the name Hoffmann translates to 'God's friend'.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing companionship with the divine.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hoffmann has a rich cultural heritage stemming from the Germanic tradition. It was a common name in Medieval Europe and increasingly popular during the early modern period. Hoffmann is also the name of a famous German author, E.T.A. Hoffmann, whose works have left an indelible mark on the literary world, particularly in the fields of romance, the supernatural, and illusion. The story of "Nutcracker and the Mouse King" is one of his most notable masterpieces that continues to be popular to this day.
data.spiritual_significance: As a compound German name, Hoffmann signifies the belief in the unity of God's presence within one's household and one's own person. The name is a humble reminder that the Divine is not confined to a temple or a monastery, but present in our homes and lives. Hence, Hoffmann means 'friend of God' or 'God's companion', encouraging the bearer to live in concert with God's will, a life filled with faith, hope, and love.
